source: Constitute Project (Comparative Constitutions Project), CC BY-NC 3.0; topic ontology and section tags are theirs

topics.label: Constitution amendment procedure
topics.desc: Details the way in which the text of the constitution can be formally amended. This is distinct from the task of constitutional interpretation often undertaken by courts.

topics.label: Establishment of cabinet/ministers
topics.desc: The body of high ranking officials who act as the heads of government departments and advise the head of state or head of government.

topics.label: Structure of the courts
topics.desc: Establishes the basic organization of the judicial branch. In some cases only the highest court is established, leaving further organization to be determined by ordinary legislation.

topics.label: Emergency provisions
topics.desc: Allows the government to declare an exceptional state, such as emergency, siege, or martial law. Usually gives the government additional powers, and may suspend some normal functions of the political system.

topics.label: Preamble
topics.desc: An introductory section which may or may not be considered an enforceable part of the constitution.

topics.label: Structure of legislative chamber(s)
topics.desc: Establishes the number of chambers in the legislature.

topics.label: General guarantee of equality
topics.desc: Guarantees that all individuals are entitled to the same privileges and immunities. Prohibits favoritism or discrimination to any group. All are considered to be equal before the law.

topics.label: Head of state powers
topics.desc: Specific, enumerated powers that are given to the head of state. For example, some heads of state are given the power to issue currency, grant asylum, award decorations, or various other particular powers.

topics.label: Head of state selection
topics.desc: The procedure through which a candidate for the office of head of state is nominated and approved. While there is great variation, common procedures include heredity, direct election, or election by the legislature.

topics.label: First chamber selection
topics.desc: Describes the procedure through which members of the first chamber of the legislature are elected or appointed.

topics.label: Immunity of legislators
topics.desc: Protection, whether absolute or limited, against prosecution for members of the legislature. This may involve protection against prosecution for certain kinds of crimes, or for a specified period of time.

topics.label: Freedom of religion
topics.desc: Grants individuals the right to hold religious beliefs, and to freely practice those religious beliefs. This right is also commonly understood to include the right to change one's religion, or to have no religion at all.

topics.label: Name/structure of executive(s)
topics.desc: Distinguishes the structure of the executive. Establishes the offices of head of state and/or head of government.

topics.label: Right to privacy
topics.desc: Grants individuals protection against government intrusion into their property, papers, person, or communications without proper authorization. Also protects against such intrusions by private individuals.

topics.label: Oaths to abide by constitution
topics.desc: Requires certain public office holders to take an oath to support or abide by the constitution.

topics.label: Source of constitutional authority
topics.desc: Establishes the agent with the authority to install the constitution or from which the state derives its ultimate authority. Many constitutions invoke the people, an assembly, a group of subnational units, a monarch, or a deity.

topics.label: Approval or veto of general legislation
topics.desc: The power to approve or reject legislation, in whole or in part, after it has been passed by the legislature. Some systems do not require this final step.

topics.label: Transitional provisions
topics.desc: Temporary sections of the constitution that guide the transition from the previous system to the current constitutional order.

topics.label: Leader of first chamber
topics.desc: Names the office that presides over the first chamber of the legislature. This function might be fulfilled by the head of government, a member of the chamber, the deputy executive, or another official.

topics.label: Motives for writing constitution
topics.desc: Frames the constitution in a particular context. Often a response to the country's recent history.

topics.label: Attorney general
topics.desc: The office responsible for representing the government in criminal or civil cases. The office may have various names, including the public prosecutor, or prosecutor general.

topics.label: Budget bills
topics.desc: Special legislative processes for budget bills, which may include restrictions on proposal, approval, or amendment. Budget bills refer to legislation that lays out the revenues and expenditures for some period of time, usually in years.

topics.label: Freedom of assembly
topics.desc: Grants individuals the right to gather in groups, in public spaces, for any otherwise legal purpose. This is right is closely associated with the idea of protest.

topics.label: Legislative committees
topics.desc: The constitution establishes the existence of legislative committees.  Sometimes details on formation and procedure are provided.

topics.label: Freedom of association
topics.desc: Grants individuals the right to form groups or associations for any otherwise legal purpose. This also sometimes includes the right not to join or associate with a group.

topics.label: Municipal government
topics.desc: Establishes the organs of municipal or local government, and their competencies.

topics.label: Freedom of expression
topics.desc: Grants individuals the right to express their thoughts and feelings without prior censorship or other forms of governmental interference. This right is rarely absolute, and is often limited in cases of sedition, hate speech, or obscenity.

topics.label: International law
topics.desc: Reference to international law, including treaties, agreements, norms, or other commitments.

topics.label: Eligibility for first chamber
topics.desc: Qualifications that an individual must meet in order to serve as a representative in the first chamber of the legislature. These often concern residency, proficiency in the official language, or prior occupation.

topics.label: Head of state removal
topics.desc: In cases where the head of state has committed a crime, or lost the confidence of the legislature, he or she may be removed from office. This may be carried out by the legislature, the head of government, or another competent body.

topics.label: Requirements for birthright citizenship
topics.desc: Details the requirements for an individual to be granted citizenship at birth. The requirements may relate to the citizenship or residency of one or both parents, or to the location of an individual's birth.

topics.label: Head of state replacement
topics.desc: The procedure by which the head of state is replaced in the event that he or she does not complete his or her term. This might involve a predetermined succession, or reversion to the normal selection procedure.

topics.label: Cabinet removal
topics.desc: Cabinet members generally serve at the pleasure of the appointing power, typically the executive. Many constitutions also allow the legislative branch to remove cabinet members in cases of misconduct.

topics.label: Establishment of judicial council
topics.desc: Establishes a special body to monitor judges. Judicial councils are commonly tasked with reviewing complaints about judges, and are sometimes involved in selecting, promoting, and removing judges.

topics.label: Removal of individual legislators
topics.desc: Procedures for removing individual members of the legislature for crimes or malfeasance. In some cases this action is taken by the legislator's chamber.

topics.label: Protection of environment
topics.desc: Imposes a duty on the state or on the people to protect or conserve the environment. This may also accord to citizens the right to enjoy a healthy environment.

topics.label: Freedom of movement
topics.desc: Grants citizens the right to travel and reside anywhere within the state, and to travel to and from other countries. The right does not normally grant non-citizens access to the state.

topics.label: Powers of cabinet
topics.desc: Matters on which the executive’s ministers have the power to act. These powers are often expressed in very general terms, but in some cases additional powers are enumerated for exercise in particular contexts.

topics.label: Restrictions on voting
topics.desc: Even where voting is considered to be a universal right, there may be some qualifications. For example, restrictions on the basis of residency, age, or criminal convictions are common.

topics.label: Eligibility for head of state
topics.desc: Qualifications that an individual must meet in order to serve as the head of government. This is sometimes as simple as eligibility to vote, but may include a number of requirements.

topics.label: Constitutionality of legislation
topics.desc: Procedures for examining whether the content of a piece of legislation is in accord with the constitution. This may or may not be permissible prior to the promulgation of the legislation.

topics.label: Protection from expropriation
topics.desc: Protects individuals and businesses from government confiscation of their property without proper compensation. The level of compensation may be variously specified as fair, full, appropriate, adequate, or otherwise.

topics.label: Right to culture
topics.desc: Establishes the right of individuals to practice their culture. May also require the state to protect or promote cultural rights.

topics.label: Subsidiary unit government
topics.desc: Specifies the competencies of the governments of the subsidiary units in a federal system.

topics.label: Type of government envisioned
topics.desc: A description of the system of government that the constitution is intended to create. Could be a description of the structure of the state, or of the political system.

topics.label: Constitutional interpretation
topics.desc: Describes which bodies of government are empowered to interpret the constitution. This is commonly the role of a constitutional court or supreme court, but in some cases is a responsibility of all or a part of the legislature.

topics.label: Referenda
topics.desc: Provides citizens an opportunity to vote for or against a specific piece of proposed legislation. Referenda are proposed by one or more bodies of the government.

topics.label: Equality regardless of gender
topics.desc: Requires that everyone is treated equally before the law, without regard to their gender or sex. This may apply to both public and private interactions in some jurisdictions.

topics.label: Right to life
topics.desc: Establishes a right to life. The precise meaning of this provision varies between jurisdictions, and may or may not be a reference to the unborn.

topics.label: Eligibility for cabinet
topics.desc: Qualifications that an individual must meet in order to serve in the cabinet. This is sometimes as simple as eligibility to vote, but may include a number of requirements. Ministers may also be restricted from serving as legislators.

topics.label: God or other deities
topics.desc: An invocation of the divine. Often found in the preamble, particularly in states with an established religion.

topics.label: Treaty ratification
topics.desc: The steps that the government must follow to gain approval for accession to a treaty. Commonly this involves gaining the consent of part or all of the legislature.

topics.label: Protection from unjustified restraint
topics.desc: Protects individuals from arbitrary detention or improper arrests. Sometimes specified as a right to a writ of habeas corpus.

topics.label: Official or national languages
topics.desc: Establishes the official languages of the state. Official languages are those used for interactions with state agencies. National languages are often local languages, while the official languages of the state sometimes include the language of a former colonial power.

topics.label: Regulation of evidence collection
topics.desc: Regulates the state's actions with regard to searches and seizures, particularly with regard to criminal investigations. May also prohibit the admission of involuntary confessions, or other suspect forms of evidence.

topics.label: Freedom of opinion/thought/conscience
topics.desc: Grants individuals the right to believe or think anything they find compelling. This does not necessarily mean that they have a right to express these beliefs.

topics.label: Freedom of press
topics.desc: Grants individuals, especially journalists and publishers, the right to free expression through all forms of media. In many jurisdictions this includes a protection against prior censorship.

topics.label: Human dignity
topics.desc: Considered one of the fundamental values of many states. Often mentioned in the preamble as a motivation for the constitution. Also a justification for some constitutional provisions.

topics.label: Legislative oversight of the executive
topics.desc: Mechanisms that allow the legislative branch to ensure that executive agencies are enforcing the laws according to the intent of the legislature. Also provides a check on the misuse or abuse of executive power.

topics.label: Initiation of general legislation
topics.desc: Specifies who has the power to propose new legislation. Beyond members of the legislature, this may or may not be extended to political parties, the general public, the head of government, or the head of state.

topics.label: Supreme/ordinary court judge removal
topics.desc: In cases where a judge has committed a crime, or otherwise compromised the integrity of their office, he or she may be removed from office. This may be carried out by the legislature, the executive, or another competent body.

topics.label: Quorum for legislative sessions
topics.desc: The legislature is only permitted to conduct its business, especially to vote on legislation, when a certain percentage of its members are present.

topics.label: Right to health care
topics.desc: Obligates the state to provide health care to its citizens, or provides individuals with the general right to health care.  In some cases, health care must be provided by the government free of charge.

topics.label: Right to own property
topics.desc: Allows individuals and corporations the sole ownership of real property, effects, financial instruments, or other objects. This right is in some cases open to violation in the interests of the community.

topics.label: Term length for first chamber
topics.desc: The number of years that a representative in the first chamber of the legislature serves before reelection, reappointment, or dismissal is required.

topics.label: Rights of children
topics.desc: Children are guaranteed certain rights or afforded special protections, which may include state-provided education and healthcare, and/or the right to be free from any kind of abuse.

topics.label: Judicial independence
topics.desc: An explicit declaration that judges are autonomous or the judiciary as a whole is independent. This may include protection from outside influence on their decision making, particularly from other branches of the government.

topics.label: Prohibition of slavery
topics.desc: Forbids the practice of owning or otherwise exploiting human beings. May still allow for compulsory labor as a punishment for a crime, and/or compulsory service in the military in time of war.

topics.label: Outside professions of legislators
topics.desc: May bar legislators from engaging in other occupations during their term in office. Limitations might include prohibitions on holding some or all other public offices, or engaging in private business.

topics.label: Deputy executive
topics.desc: Specification of the deputy to the head of state or head of government. The deputy executive typically has the power to act when the executive is absent or becomes incapable of holding office.

topics.label: National flag
topics.desc: Describes the principal features of the national flag.

topics.label: Advisory bodies to the head of state
topics.desc: In addition to a cabinet, other councils of high ranking officials may advise the head of state. This could include a privy council to a monarch, for example. Some advisory bodies may consult on specific topics, such as national security.

topics.label: Dismissal of the legislature
topics.desc: Specifies who has the authority to dismiss the legislature. May also specify the conditions under which this may take place.

topics.label: Ownership of natural resources
topics.desc: Describes ownership of natural resources in general, or makes specific references to ownership or use of energy, mineral, water, flora, fauna, or other natural resources.

topics.label: Head of government removal
topics.desc: In cases where the head of government has committed a crime, or lost the confidence of the legislature, he or she may be removed from office. This may be carried out by the legislature, the head of state, or another competent body.

topics.label: Right to join trade unions
topics.desc: Grants individuals the right to form and join trade unions or professional associations. This is an explicit right that goes beyond freedom of association.

topics.label: Supreme court selection
topics.desc: The procedure through which a candidate for a supreme court judgeship is nominated and approved.  This might involve approval from the executive, and all or part of the legislature.

topics.label: Head of state term length
topics.desc: The number of years that a head of state serves before either reappointment or dismissal is required.

topics.label: Prohibition of cruel treatment
topics.desc: Forbids the state from treating individuals in a way that offends the principle of human dignity. This may include forms of corporal or capital punishment, excessive delays in assessing punishment, or other actions prejudicial to the rights of offenders.

topics.label: Secret ballot
topics.desc: Voting takes place in such a way that a citizen completes the ballot privately, and the ballot cannot be connected to the voter.

topics.label: Head of state immunity
topics.desc: Protection, whether absolute or limited, against prosecution for the head of state. This may involve protection against prosecution for certain kinds of crimes, or for a specified period of time.

topics.label: Power to pardon
topics.desc: Gives a body within the executive branch the authority to overrule a criminal conviction.

topics.label: Right of petition
topics.desc: Grants groups and individuals the right to bring petitions to the government. This includes the right to bring complaints about the actions of the government.

topics.label: Equality regardless of race
topics.desc: Requires that everyone is treated equally before the law, without regard to their race. This may apply to both public and private interactions in some jurisdictions.

topics.label: Prohibition of torture
topics.desc: Forbids the state from torturing individuals, and in some cases from using coerced statements in court.  This prohibition may be limited in cases of war or other circumstances.

topics.label: Legal status of treaties
topics.desc: This especially concerns the status of treaties with regard to the constitution or ordinary law, and determines whether treaties are superior or inferior to the constitution or ordinary law.

topics.label: National capital
topics.desc: Names the capital city of the state.

topics.label: Reference to science
topics.desc: Reference to science, which may include prioritization of investment in scientific research, or mandate state support for science and innovation.

topics.label: Requirements for naturalization
topics.desc: Naturalization is the process through which a person acquires a citizenship to which they did not have a right by birth. These provisions detail the requirements an individual must fulfil in order to gain citizenship.

topics.label: Right to work
topics.desc: Gives citizens a general right to work, and/or obligates the state to provide work. This is distinct from the right to choose one's occupation.

topics.label: State support for the disabled
topics.desc: Obligates the state to provide financial or material resources to persons with disabilities.

topics.label: Designation of commander in chief
topics.desc: Establishes ultimate control of the state's armed forces. Usually the head of state or head of government. This may be a ceremonial role, or may involve significant decision-making power.

topics.label: Extraordinary legislative sessions
topics.desc: Establishes who has the authority to call an extraordinary session of the legislature, and in some cases what circumstances would allow them to take such action.

topics.label: Ultra-vires administrative actions
topics.desc: Protects individuals from the use of excess power by administrative agencies of the government. Commonly also establishes procedures for review of such actions and provides redress for those harmed.

topics.label: Electoral commission
topics.desc: An independent commission responsible for facilitating and regulating elections. May be responsible for monitoring political parties and the financing of elections.

topics.label: Conditions for revoking citizenship
topics.desc: Describes the conditions under which a government is allowed to revoke an individual's citizenship. Some constitutions expressly forbid the government from revoking citizenship, regardless of the circumstances.

topics.label: Reference to art
topics.desc: References to art or artists indicate the importance of art to the national identity, and are often made in the context of mandating state support for the arts.

topics.label: Claim of universal suffrage
topics.desc: The right to vote is held by all citizens. There may nevertheless be some restrictions on voting by residency, age, residency or criminal conviction.

topics.label: International organizations
topics.desc: Reference to international organizations, whether generally or with regard to specific international organizations such as the United Nations.

topics.label: Size of first chamber
topics.desc: The total number of seats in the first chamber of the legislature.

topics.label: Equality regardless of religion
topics.desc: Requires that everyone is treated equally before the law, without regard to their religion. This may apply to both public and private interactions in some jurisdictions.

topics.label: National anthem
topics.desc: Names the official anthem of the state.

topics.label: Supreme court powers
topics.desc: Establishes the competencies of the supreme court, other than adjudication and review of legislation. Such powers may include supervision of elections, impeachment of the executive, review of treaties, or other specified functions.

topics.label: Cabinet selection
topics.desc: Establishes the bodies competent to nominate and approve members of the cabinet. Appointment is usually made by the executive branch, and is in some cases subject to approval by the legislative branch.

topics.label: Head of state decree power
topics.desc: Allows the head of state to enact rules without following the usual channels for the passage of legislation. This power is usually limited to particular circumstances or areas of government activity.

topics.label: Establishment of constitutional court
topics.desc: A court that is especially empowered to interpret the constitution, and usually to rule on whether legislation is in accord with the principles of the constitution.

topics.label: Head of government selection
topics.desc: The procedure through which a candidate for the office of head of government is nominated and approved. This typically involves approval from both the legislature and the head of state.

topics.label: Principle of no punishment without law
topics.desc: Protects individuals from being prosecuted for actions that were not crimes at the time they were committed. Similarly, the sentence imposed cannot be greater than the one that was mandated at the time that the crime was committed.

topics.label: Reference to fraternity/solidarity
topics.desc: Considered one of the fundamental values of many states. Often mentioned in the preamble as a motivation for the constitution.

topics.label: Right to appeal judicial decisions
topics.desc: Gives individuals the right to appeal a judicial decision in a higher court if they are not satisfied with the outcome in the court of first instance. Does not necessarily require the appellate court to hear the case, but the mention of an appellate court may imply the power to appeal.

topics.label: Replacement of legislators
topics.desc: Establishes the procedure through which a seat in the legislature may be filled in the event that a legislator has been removed from office, resigns, or dies.

topics.label: Protection from ex post facto laws
topics.desc: Protects individuals from prosecution for acts that were not criminal at the time that they were committed, or from changes in the penalties for acts.

topics.label: Public or private sessions
topics.desc: Specifies whether the legislature is to conduct its business in public or in private. When legislative sessions are generally public, some constitutions may also specify the conditions (if any) under which the legislature may hold private sessions.

topics.label: Duty to serve in the military
topics.desc: A duty to serve a specified period of time in the country's military. Often also includes protections for conscientious objectors.

topics.label: Length of legislative sessions
topics.desc: The number of days or months that the legislature meets within a year.

topics.label: Ombudsman
topics.desc: A public official tasked with investigating improper or illegal actions on the part of government agencies which may infringe on the rights of individuals. Enables individuals to bring complaints about the actions of the government.

topics.label: Right to form political parties
topics.desc: Establishes the right to join a party or other political organization, or gives citizens the right to form new political parties.

topics.label: Right to information
topics.desc: Grants individuals access to information collected or held by the government, particularly information about oneself, or information of general public interest.

topics.label: Scheduling of elections
topics.desc: When elections shall be held. This could be described in terms of a particular day, an interval between elections, or with relation to the dismissal of the legislature or executive.

topics.label: Ordinary court selection
topics.desc: The procedure through which a candidate for an ordinary court judgeship is nominated and approved.  This might involve approval from the executive, and all or part of the legislature.

topics.label: State support for children
topics.desc: Obligates the state to provide financial or material resources to children.

topics.label: State support for the elderly
topics.desc: Obligates the state to provide financial or material resources to elderly persons.

topics.label: Central bank
topics.desc: Establishes or affirms a central bank. May also include requirements for its governance and operations.

topics.label: Constitutional court powers
topics.desc: Establishes the competencies of the constitutional court, other than adjudication and review of legislation. Such powers may include supervision of elections, impeachment of the executive, review of treaties, or other specified functions.

topics.label: Free education
topics.desc: Requires the state to provide education free of charge. This may be limited at a certain age or level of educational attainment.

topics.label: Reference to country's history
topics.desc: May invoke particular triumphs or tragedies in the country's past. Situates the constitution in the country's larger legal and political identity.

topics.label: Division of labor between chambers
topics.desc: Specifies the manner in which the work of the legislative process is divided between the two chambers of the legislature. For example, legislation could be considered concurrently or sequentially, or could be divided on the basis of policy areas.

topics.label: Duty to obey the constitution
topics.desc: Requires citizens or public officers to obey the constitution. This primarily applies to individuals in cases where the constitution includes a statement of the duties of citizens or holders of public office.

topics.label: Inalienable rights
topics.desc: Rights that are understood to be unassailable, either because they are fundamental or “natural.”  In some countries, they may be absolute rights, not subject even to qualification.

topics.label: Right to counsel
topics.desc: Gives individuals who have been arrested the right to legal counsel. In absence of a right to counsel some constitutions grant only the right to a defense.

topics.label: Foreign affairs representative
topics.desc: Indicates the government official or body authorized to speak for the state abroad. This function could be fulfilled by the head of state, or by another government official such as the foreign minister.

topics.label: Veto override procedure
topics.desc: Allows the legislature to take additional steps to pass legislation that has been vetoed by the actor responsible for approving or rejecting legislation. This typically requires a supermajority, but there is some variation.

topics.label: Compensation of legislators
topics.desc: Specifies the actors involved in establishing the compensation of legislators. In addition to the legislature, this might involve the head of state, head of government, an independent commission, or other actors.

topics.label: Right to found a family
topics.desc: Grants individuals the right to commit to one another and raise children together. This right is closely tied to the right to marry. Many constitutions stipulate only a general state duty to protect the family.

topics.label: Equality regardless of origin
topics.desc: Requires that everyone is treated equally before the law, without regard to their country or place of origin. This may apply to both public and private interactions in some jurisdictions.

topics.label: Age restrictions on head of state
topics.desc: Most commonly establishes the minimum age that an individual must have attained before assuming the office of head of state. In some cases may also provide a maximum age.

topics.label: Regional group(s)
topics.desc: Reference to a group of states, a geographical region, or an intergovernmental organization, such as the European Union.

topics.label: Equality regardless of creed or belief
topics.desc: Requires that everyone is treated equally before the law, without regard to their creed, belief, or opinions. This may apply to both public and private interactions in some jurisdictions.

topics.label: Head of state term limits
topics.desc: The number of terms, either consecutive or in total, that an individual may serve in the office of head of state

topics.label: Protection of stateless persons
topics.desc: Requires the state to offer its protection to one or more of the following vulnerable groups: stateless persons, asylum seekers, or refugees.

topics.label: Right to strike
topics.desc: Grants individuals and groups the right to cease work for a period of time, in an effort to exert pressure on their employer. This may or may not include protection for the jobs of strikers.

topics.label: Second chamber selection
topics.desc: Describes the procedure through which members of the second chamber of the legislature are elected or appointed. This is often different from the selection procedure used for the first chamber.

topics.label: Compulsory education
topics.desc: Requires children to attend school. This may be a requirement up to a certain age, or to a certain level of educational attainment.

topics.label: Electoral districts
topics.desc: Describes characteristics, or rules for the establishment, of electoral districts. Constitutions rarely directly establish the districts, but rather describe where and how these decisions will be made.

topics.label: Equality regardless of political party
topics.desc: Requires that everyone is treated equally before the law, without regard to their political party membership or political opinions. This may apply to both public and private interactions in some jurisdictions.

topics.label: Right to choose occupation
topics.desc: Grants individuals the freedom to choose their occupation and their place of employment without interference from the government.

topics.label: Right to public trial
topics.desc: Grants individuals charged with an offense the right to have their trial held in public.

topics.label: Supreme court term length
topics.desc: The number of years that a supreme court justice serves before either reappointment or dismissal is required.

topics.label: Unamendable provisions
topics.desc: Some provisions in the constitutions may be so fundamental to the constitutional order, or so politically contentious, that they are designated as unamendable. In such cases, unamendable provisions are expressly noted in the constitution.

topics.label: Power to declare/approve war
topics.desc: The process that the government must follow in order to establish a declaration of war. For example, this could be a power of the head of state, of the cabinet as a whole, or it could require consent from the legislative branch.

topics.label: Protection of language use
topics.desc: Protects the right of individuals to use their native language, or otherwise provides general protections for particular languages. Protected languages may be specified, but remain distinct from the official languages of the state.

topics.label: Restrictions on political parties
topics.desc: Establishes the boundaries of acceptable activity, or the organizational structure, of political parties. For example, parties may be bound to respect some fundamental principles of the state.

topics.label: Head of government powers
topics.desc: Specific, enumerated powers that are given to the head of government. For example, some heads of government are given the power to issue currency, grant asylum, award decorations, or various other particular powers.

topics.label: Official religion
topics.desc: Establishment of an official religion, or religions, for the state. Other constitutions provide special treatment for certain religions, or conversely, expressly forbid the state from establishing an official religion.

topics.label: Tax bills
topics.desc: Special legislative processes for tax bills, which may include restrictions on proposal, approval, or amendment. Tax bills refer to legislation specifically for collecting revenue for public use, usually in the form of taxes or tariffs.

topics.label: Age restrictions on first chamber
topics.desc: Most commonly establishes the minimum age that an individual must have attained to be eligible to serve as a representative in the first chamber of the legislature. In some cases may also provide a maximum age.

topics.label: Eligibility for second chamber
topics.desc: Qualifications that an individual must meet in order to serve as a representative in the second chamber of the legislature. These often concern residency, proficiency in the official language, or prior occupation.

topics.label: Extradition procedure
topics.desc: Details the procedure that must be followed for the state to surrender an individual apprehended on its territory to the government of another state for criminal proceedings. Where permitted, this is usually further regulated through bi-lateral treaties.

topics.label: Right to shelter
topics.desc: Grants individuals the right to adequate shelter or housing. Often framed in terms of facilitating family life.

topics.label: Constitutional court selection
topics.desc: The procedure through which a candidate for a constitutional court judgeship is nominated and approved.  This might involve approval from the executive, and all or part of the legislature.

topics.label: Eligibility for supreme court judges
topics.desc: Qualifications that an individual must meet in order to serve as a judge on the supreme court. These often concern educational and professional credentials.

topics.label: Presumption of innocence in trials
topics.desc: Requires that those adjudicating a criminal trial maintain the posture that the accused is "innocent until proven guilty." This places the burden of proof on the side of the prosecution in the trial.

topics.label: Equality regardless of skin color
topics.desc: Requires that everyone is treated equally before the law, without regard to their skin color. This may apply to both public and private interactions in some jurisdictions.

topics.label: Leader of second chamber
topics.desc: Names the office that presides over the second chamber of the legislature. This function might be fulfilled by a member of the chamber, the deputy executive, or another official.

topics.label: Right to establish a business
topics.desc: Grants individuals the right to establish for-profit commercial endeavors.

topics.label: Spending bills
topics.desc: Special legislative processes for spending bills, which may include restrictions on proposal, approval, or amendment. Spending bills refer to legislation specifically for the expenditure of government money.

topics.label: Duty to pay taxes
topics.desc: Requires all citizens to contribute to the expenses of the state through taxes. This is usually a general statement and may still allow for variation on the basis of income.

topics.label: Right to reasonable standard of living
topics.desc: Grants individuals the right to a standard of living that sustains human dignity. May also refer to adequate well-being, suitable existence, or life worthy of a human being.

topics.label: Equality regardless of social status
topics.desc: Requires that everyone is treated equally before the law, without regard to their social status or origin. This may apply to both public and private interactions in some jurisdictions.

topics.label: Right to academic freedom
topics.desc: Allows scholars to pursue their research agenda without undue interference from the state. This is usually understood to also include freedom to teach and publish.

topics.label: Right to fair trial
topics.desc: Protects individuals from unfair procedures. Fair trials often require a public hearing within a reasonable time following the arrest, and judgment by a competent and impartial jury.

topics.label: Eligibility for head of government
topics.desc: Qualifications that an individual must meet in order to serve as the head of government. This is sometimes as simple as eligibility to vote, but may include a number of requirements.

topics.label: Equality regardless of language
topics.desc: Requires that everyone is treated equally before the law, without regard to their language. This may apply to both public and private interactions in some jurisdictions.

topics.label: Joint meetings of legislative chambers
topics.desc: Provides for the two chambers of a bicameral legislature to meet jointly. This may involve a body made up of both chambers, or a special joint session for specific purposes.

topics.label: Provisions for intellectual property
topics.desc: Gives individuals and businesses the exclusive right to protect and profit from their creative works.

topics.label: Regulation of marriage
topics.desc: Regulates marriage, including granting the right to marry and establishing rules regarding divorce. May include a definition of marriage, and may or may not be limited to heterosexual couples.

topics.label: Restrictions on the armed forces
topics.desc: Limitations either on the government's use of the military, or on the actions of members of the military. For example, prohibition of domestic deployment of the military, or restrictions on the political rights of military officers.

topics.label: Right to just remuneration
topics.desc: Grants individuals the right to just remuneration or fair/equal payment for work. May also regulate wages including the establishment of a minimum or living wage.

topics.label: Separation of church and state
topics.desc: Guarantees separation between the state and religious organizations. The state may be forbidden from extending governmental recognition or assistance to religious organizations.

topics.label: Telecommunications
topics.desc: Reference to wired or wireless communication, and the industries that support it, usually in the context of regulation. Includes telephones, satellites, the internet, and other communication technologies.

topics.label: Right to competitive marketplace
topics.desc: Protects individuals and businesses from monopolies, price fixing, and other means of reducing competition in the marketplace.

topics.label: Standing committees
topics.desc: Establishes permanent committees with oversight in given policy areas, which often exercise legislative authority when the legislature is not in session. May also specify how members of these committees are selected, and how long they serve.

topics.label: Eligibility for const court judges
topics.desc: Qualifications that an individual must meet in order to serve as a judge in a constitutional court. These often concern educational and professional credentials.

topics.label: Establishment of military courts
topics.desc: Courts with jurisdiction limited to charges against members of the military, and tasked with enforcing military law.

topics.label: Integration of ethnic communities
topics.desc: Minority ethnic communities are enabled to participate in the affairs of the state or society. Some constitutions offer additional protection against forced assimilation.

topics.label: Prohibition of capital punishment
topics.desc: Forbids the state from employing the death penalty as a punishment for any crime.

topics.label: Right to transfer property
topics.desc: Grants the right to dispose of property through sale, gift, private wills, or other means.

topics.label: Constitutional court term length
topics.desc: The number of years that a constitutional court judge serves before either reappointment or dismissal is required.

topics.label: First chamber reserved policy areas
topics.desc: Names specific areas of legislation that are a special concern for the first chamber. This may include sole authority to legislate in these areas.

topics.label: Customary international law
topics.desc: Reference to customary international law, the law of nations, or the generally accepted principles of international law.

topics.label: Rights or duties of parents
topics.desc: Grants parents certain rights or duties regarding their children. May include the duty to provide for one's legal children, or the right to make decisions about their education, upbringing, and other aspects of their lives.

topics.label: Selection of active-duty commanders
topics.desc: The selection process for the highest ranking officers in the military. This often involves appointment by the head of the executive branch, and in some cases also requires the approval of at least part of the legislature.

topics.label: Establishment of administrative courts
topics.desc: Courts that adjudicate disputes about the government's exercise of power in ordinary administrative functions.

topics.label: International human rights treaties
topics.desc: Reference to one or more specific international treaties or instruments concerning human rights.

topics.label: Protection from false imprisonment
topics.desc: Provides redress for individuals who have been confined or arrested without just cause, or have otherwise suffered from judicial error.

topics.label: Finance bills
topics.desc: Special legislative processes for finance bills, which may include restrictions on proposal, approval, or amendment. Finance bills refer to legislation specifically for the borrowing of money for governmental use, like loans from NGOs, other countries, or even private individuals.

topics.label: Protection of consumers
topics.desc: Addresses consumer rights or consumer protection. Protects consumers from harmful products and/or predatory or unethical business practices.

topics.label: State support for the unemployed
topics.desc: Obligates the state to provide financial or material resources to unemployed persons.

topics.label: Term length of second chamber
topics.desc: The number of years that a representative in the second chamber of the legislature serves before reelection, reappointment, or dismissal is required.

topics.label: National vs subnational laws
topics.desc: Establishes which level of government has supremacy on certain legislative matters or in cases where their laws are in conflict.

topics.label: Protection from self-incrimination
topics.desc: Grants individuals the right to forego answering questions during an interrogation or in court that would tend to confirm the individual's guilt. In some cases an individual may waive this right if they so choose.

topics.label: Radio
topics.desc: Reference to the wireless transmission of audio programs, usually in the context of regulation.

topics.label: Right to rest and leisure
topics.desc: Grants individuals the right to vacations, weekly holidays, and/or annual paid vacation. May be provided via regulation of working hours.

topics.label: Television
topics.desc: Reference to the wireless transmission of audio-visual programs, usually in the context of regulation.

topics.label: Head of government replacement
topics.desc: The procedure by which the head of government is replaced in the event that he or she does not complete his or her term. This might involve a predetermined succession, or reversion to the normal selection procedure.

topics.label: Human rights commission
topics.desc: An independent commission tasked with investigating potential violations of human rights. The commission may be empowered to take action, or may be required to forward its findings to the regular courts.

topics.label: Limits on employment of children
topics.desc: Protects children against exploitation in the workplace. This may be in the form of a ban on child workers, or as a requirement for additional protections for child workers.

topics.label: Mentions of social class
topics.desc: Explicit references to social class. This may be in the context of either outlawing or providing for a system of social classes within the state, or in the context of pursuing socio-economic equality.

topics.label: Right to protect one's reputation
topics.desc: Grants individuals the right to defend themselves against libel or slander. Understood in the context of freedom of expression, this may not include prior censorship, allowing instead for legal remedy after the fact.

topics.label: Accession of territory
topics.desc: Allows the state to incorporate new territory into the country. Usually also specifies the necessary steps for this to happen.

topics.label: Head of government decree power
topics.desc: Allows the head of government, or exceptionally the cabinet, to enact rules without following the usual channels for the passage of legislation. This power is usually limited to particular circumstances or areas of government activity.

topics.label: Protection of judges' salaries
topics.desc: Prevents tampering with the salaries of judges for political ends. Can bolster judicial independence.  Provisions about protection of the overall judicial budget are included here.

topics.label: Right to speedy trial
topics.desc: Grants individuals charged with an offense the right to be brought to trial without any undue delay.

topics.label: Eligibility for ordinary court judges
topics.desc: Qualifications that an individual must meet in order to serve as a judge in an ordinary court. These often concern educational and professional credentials.

topics.label: Civil service recruitment
topics.desc: Requires that officials in the public service are recruited and promoted on the basis of merit. This is intended to be a hedge against patronage and nepotism, and may require standardized exams or a specified kind of credential.

topics.label: Equality for persons with disabilities
topics.desc: Requires that everyone is treated equally before the law, without regard to any disability. This may apply to both public and private interactions in some jurisdictions.

topics.label: Head of government's role in the legislature
topics.desc: Establishes whether the head of government is required to serve, or is prohibited from serving, as a member of the legislature.

topics.label: Legislative initiatives by citizens
topics.desc: Allows private citizens to propose new legislation. Usually this requires additional qualifications, such as support from a political party, a member of the legislature, or a certain number of signatures from other citizens.

topics.label: Publication of deliberations
topics.desc: Requires that a written record of the deliberations of the legislature be published.

topics.label: State operation of the media
topics.desc: Describes the relationship between the state and the media. This may give the state control over all media, allow the state to operate some media, or prohibit the state from such activities.

topics.label: Campaign financing
topics.desc: Rules that political parties and candidates must follow in financing electoral campaigns. Some constitutions establish government assistance for such purposes, or forbid receipt of funds from certain other sources.

topics.label: Prohibition of double jeopardy
topics.desc: Prohibits the state from charging an individual with an offense for which they have already been acquitted. This does not necessarily prevent the prosecution from appealing an acquittal.

topics.label: Provision for matrimonial equality
topics.desc: Gives both spouses the same rights in marriage and family law. This is a separate issue from the general guarantee of gender equality.

topics.label: Number of supreme court judges
topics.desc: Establishes the number of seats on the supreme court.

topics.label: Right to renounce citizenship
topics.desc: Grants individuals the right to renounce their citizenship. This right is sometimes subject to qualifications relating to dual-citizenship, or the existence of a state of war.

topics.label: Mandatory retirement age for judges
topics.desc: Specifies the age at which judges must step down. A common alternative to term limits.

topics.label: Restrictions on entry or exit
topics.desc: Primarily concerned with the movements of foreign nationals, describes the powers of the government to restrict entry into or exit out of the state.

topics.label: Prohibited political parties
topics.desc: Certain political parties, or parties with particular ideologies or characteristics, are prohibited. For example, some constitutions prohibit parties that are founded on a tribal or group identity.

topics.label: Right to safe work environment
topics.desc: Grants individuals the right to work in environments free of preventable hazards. This may include an obligation on the state to provide safe working conditions, or to address violations thereof.

topics.label: Constitutional court removal
topics.desc: In cases where a judge has committed a crime, or otherwise compromised the integrity of their office, he or she may be removed from office. This may be carried out by the legislature, the executive, or another competent body.

topics.label: Jury trials required
topics.desc: Grants individuals the right to trial by jury, or more generally provides for citizen participation in the adjudication of guilt in criminal trials.

topics.label: Organic laws
topics.desc: Special legislative processes for organic laws, which may include restrictions on proposal, approval, or amendment. Organic laws establish fundamental aspects of the constitutional order, including establishing institutions like the courts or legislature, and in some jurisdictions are accorded similar status to the constitution itself. They sometimes require a higher standard for approval than ordinary law.

topics.label: Right to development of personality
topics.desc: Grants individuals the right to both develop and express their own unique personality.

topics.label: Size of second chamber
topics.desc: The total number of seats in the second chamber of the legislature.

topics.label: Constitutional court term limits
topics.desc: The number of terms, either consecutive or in total, that an individual may serve as a judge in a constitutional court.

topics.label: Counter corruption commission
topics.desc: An independent commission specifically empowered to investigate corruption within the government.

topics.label: Duty to work
topics.desc: Requires individuals to contribute to the betterment of their society through work. This is usually a general statement and may still allow for variation on the basis of disability, age or other factors.

topics.label: Economic plans
topics.desc: Mention of national economic plans, possibly with the procedure for establishing them. Such procedures may include special rules for proposal, approval, or amendment.

topics.label: Equality regardless of financial status
topics.desc: Requires that everyone is treated equally before the law, without regard to their financial status or property ownership. This may apply to both public and private interactions in some jurisdictions.

topics.label: Equality regardless of parentage
topics.desc: Requires that everyone is treated equally before the law, without regard to their parentage or birth. This may apply to both public and private interactions in some jurisdictions.

topics.label: Guarantee of due process
topics.desc: Ensures that defendants in criminal trials are entitled to have their cases heard according to the process established by law. This may include specific rights, such as the right to be informed of the charges, the right to counsel, and the right to appeal.

topics.label: Right to self determination
topics.desc: Establishes a group right to self determination. This may be a reference to the nation as a whole, to groups in other countries, or to a portion of the state's population.

topics.label: Supermajority required for legislation
topics.desc: Particularly vital or contentious policy areas may require a supermajority of a specified size in order to pass legislation.  Although constitutional amendments often require a supermajority, this topic addresses ordinary legislation only.

topics.label: Access to higher education
topics.desc: Guarantees individuals equal access to higher education. In some cases this may be limited on a competitive basis, or by tests of aptitude.

topics.label: Age restrictions on second chamber
topics.desc: Most commonly establishes the minimum age that an individual must have attained to be eligible to serve as a representative in the second chamber of the legislature. In some cases may also provide a maximum age.

topics.label: Ordinary court term length
topics.desc: The number of years that an ordinary court judge serves before either reappointment or dismissal is required.

topics.label: Political theorists/figures
topics.desc: Reference to historical figures or political theorists. Usually mentioned in the preamble in the context of a particular political tradition.

topics.label: Administrative court selection
topics.desc: The procedure through which a candidate for an administrative judgeship is nominated and approved. This might involve approval from the executive, and all or part of the legislature.

topics.label: National motto
topics.desc: Affirms the national motto, sometimes in more than one language.

topics.label: Census
topics.desc: Provides for the enumeration of residents periodically. Additional instructions about the conduct of the census may also be given.

topics.label: Earnings disclosure requirement
topics.desc: Requires legislators to disclose their income, or the value of their assets. This disclosure is typically made to a specified official or commission, and is not necessarily made public.

topics.label: Head of government immunity
topics.desc: Protection, whether absolute or limited, against prosecution for the head of government. This may involve protection against prosecution for certain kinds of crimes, or for a specified period of time.

topics.label: Courts for judging public officials
topics.desc: Special courts that are empowered to review the actions of public servants acting in their official capacity.

topics.label: First chamber representation quotas
topics.desc: Specifies the proportion of the seats in the first chamber that must be assigned to representatives of a particular group, such as women, ethnic groups, political parties, religious groups, or social classes.

topics.label: Provisions for wealth redistribution
topics.desc: The state is required to provide additional resources, either in monetary contributions or in services, to specific groups within the society. Categories might include gender, ethnicity, disability, or any other group identity.

topics.label: Second chamber reserved policy areas
topics.desc: Names specific areas of legislation that are a special concern for the second chamber. This may include sole authority to legislate in these areas.

topics.label: Federal review of subnational legislation
topics.desc: In federal countries, the power of the federal government to review legislation passed by the governments of the subnational units. Such review could be undertaken by a federal court or another part of the federal government.

topics.label: Right to water
topics.desc: Grants individuals the right to water. May include a guarantee of safe, clean, or potable drinking water. Often associated with a state duty to provide or protect water as a resource.

topics.label: Attendance by legislators
topics.desc: Requires legislators to attend sessions or votes. Examples include mandatory attendance, punishment after a specified number of absences, or delegating the matter to ordinary law.

topics.label: Binding effect of const rights
topics.desc: Establishes whether or not the rights listed in the constitution are binding on private individuals as well as the state.

topics.label: Media commission
topics.desc: Establishes a commission to regulate mass media. This may include ensuring free expression, and in some cases enforcing some form of censorship.

topics.label: Supreme court term limits
topics.desc: The number of terms, either consecutive or in total, that an individual may serve as a judge on the supreme court.

topics.label: Trial in native language of accused
topics.desc: Grants individuals charged with an offense the right to have their trial conducted in a language they understand, or the right to have an interpreter. In some cases, this would include a right to be informed of the reasons for one’s arrest.

topics.label: Equality regardless of nationality
topics.desc: Requires that everyone is treated equally before the law, without regard to their nationality. This may apply to both public and private interactions in some jurisdictions.

topics.label: Balanced budget
topics.desc: A requirement that the government pass a budget in which incoming revenue meets or exceeds the value of the government's expenditures in a fiscal year.

topics.label: Claim of executive independence
topics.desc: Closely related to the idea of separation of powers, this is a constitutional guarantee of the independence of the executive.

topics.label: Protection of victim's rights
topics.desc: Grants the victims of crime rights in the justice process. These rights may include attendance at the trial, an opportunity to speak at the trial, restitution, or other measures to address the needs of crime victims.

topics.label: Right to pre-trial release
topics.desc: Grants individuals who have been arrested and charged with a crime the right to be released from custody until the time of their trial. This may require paying the court a sum of money to be repaid at the time of the trial, or other conditions for release.

topics.label: Age restrictions on head of government
topics.desc: Most commonly establishes the minimum age that an individual must have attained before assuming the office of head of government. In some cases may also provide a maximum age.

topics.label: Power to deport citizens
topics.desc: In extraordinary circumstances, usually relating to criminal convictions abroad, some constitutions give the government the power to deport citizens. In other constitutions, the government is specifically prohibited from deporting citizens but allows deportation of other residents.

topics.label: Right to enjoy the benefits of science
topics.desc: Accords individuals the right to enjoy the benefits of scientific progress, or obligates the state to promote scientific advancement for the benefit of society.

topics.label: Rights of debtors
topics.desc: Protection for individuals who are unable to repay loans or other financial obligations. The contractual rights of the lender are qualified by the right of the debtor to their freedom or dignity.

topics.label: Crimes of the previous regime
topics.desc: Usually in the context of specifying the new regime's treatment of these crimes. May grant amnesty or require punishment.

topics.label: Electoral court powers
topics.desc: Establishes the competencies of the electoral court. In addition to hearing challenges of election results, the court may be responsible for certifying various aspects of elections, including voter rolls and final vote tallies.

topics.label: Indigenous right to self governance
topics.desc: Grants indigenous peoples limited rights to self-government, particularly with regard to issues that affect their territory.

topics.label: Privileges for juveniles in criminal process
topics.desc: Grants juveniles charged with crimes special protections in the judicial system. This may include special courts, different sentencing rules, or special detention centers.

topics.label: Restrictions on rights of groups
topics.desc: Explains circumstances under which the rights of some individuals or groups may be restricted.

topics.label: Right to conscientious objection
topics.desc: Grants individuals whose religious or ethical beliefs prevent them from participating in war an exemption from military service.

topics.label: Secrecy of legislative votes
topics.desc: Establishes the level of transparency in legislative voting. This could be a matter of public record, always kept secret, or varied depending on the topic of the vote.

topics.label: Status of religious law
topics.desc: Religious law and constitutional law interact in complex ways. Constitutions can treat religious law as entirely separate, integrated to some degree, applied in areas where secular law is silent, considered superior, or used as a source or inspiration for secular law.

topics.label: Equality regardless of age
topics.desc: Requires that everyone is treated equally before the law, without regard to their age. This may apply to both public and private interactions in some jurisdictions.

topics.label: Equality regardless of tribe or clan
topics.desc: Requires that everyone is treated equally before the law, without regard to their tribe or clan. This may apply to both public and private interactions in some jurisdictions.

topics.label: Judicial precedence
topics.desc: A requirement that judges must at least take into account, and potentially follow, precedents set by rulings in higher courts.

topics.label: Right to overthrow government
topics.desc: Grants citizens the right to overthrow the government under certain circumstances. This right is usually expressed in terms of defending the constitutional order, rather than establishing a new one.

topics.label: Supreme court opinions
topics.desc: Determines procedures for, or treatment of, judicial opinions handed down by the supreme court.

topics.label: Terrorism
topics.desc: Terrorism specifically mentioned, usually in the context of the criminal justice system, or with regard to the activities of the military or other public safety bodies.

topics.label: Age restrictions on supreme court judges
topics.desc: Most commonly establishes the minimum age that an individual must have attained before assuming the office of judge on the supreme court. In some cases may also provide a maximum age.

topics.label: Electoral court selection
topics.desc: The procedure through which a candidate for an electoral court judgeship is nominated and approved.  This might involve approval from the executive, and all or part of the legislature.

topics.label: Right to amparo
topics.desc: Gives citizens the right to request judicial review of government actions or judgments that they believe have violated their rights.

topics.label: Secession of territory
topics.desc: Addresses secession or withdrawal of groups or territories of the state. In cases where secession is allowed, usually also specifies the legal process that must take place.

topics.label: Eligibility for electoral court judges
topics.desc: Qualifications that an individual must meet in order to serve as a judge in an electoral court. These often concern educational and professional credentials.

topics.label: Regulation of political parties
topics.desc: Describes which branch or body of the government has the power to regulate political parties, particularly those tasked with determining the unconstitutionality of certain parties.

topics.label: Administrative court term length
topics.desc: The number of years that an administrative judge serves before either reappointment or dismissal is required.

topics.label: Drugs, alcohol, and illegal substances
topics.desc: Provisions about the regulation or criminalization of the trafficking, sale, or consumption of alcohol, drugs, or other controlled or illegal substances.

topics.label: Eligibility for administrative  judges
topics.desc: Conditions that an individual must fulfil in order to serve as a judge in an administrative court. These often concern educational and professional credentials.

topics.label: Limits on removing head of government
topics.desc: Protections from removal for the head of government. For example, a failed attempt to remove the head of government may preclude additional votes on the matter for a specified period of time.

topics.label: Right to examine evidence/witnesses
topics.desc: Grants an accused offender, and their legal counsel, the right to cross-examine evidence or witnesses brought against them by the prosecution.

topics.label: Second chamber representation quotas
topics.desc: Specifies the proportion of the seats in the second chamber that must be assigned to representatives of a particular group, such as women, ethnic groups, political parties, religious groups, or social classes.

topics.label: Prohibition of corporal punishment
topics.desc: Forbids the state from inflicting physical harm on an offender as a punishment for any crime.

topics.label: Provision for civil marriage
topics.desc: Recognizes secular marriages performed by a government official or other so empowered individuals, or religious marriages that also involve a license from the state.

topics.label: Age restrictions on constitutional court judges
topics.desc: Most commonly establishes the minimum age that an individual must have attained before assuming the office of judge in a constitutional court. In some cases may also provide a maximum age.

topics.label: Colonies
topics.desc: Mention of territory beyond the national borders that is under the government's control. This may include colonies, protectorates, or territories.

topics.label: Electoral court term length
topics.desc: The number of years that an electoral judge serves before either reappointment or dismissal is required.

topics.label: Establishment of labor courts
topics.desc: Courts with limited jurisdiction to adjudicate disputes between individuals or trade unions and businesses.

topics.label: Head of government term length
topics.desc: The number of years that a head of government serves before either reappointment or dismissal is required.

topics.label: Compulsory voting
topics.desc: Makes voting mandatory for at least some electors in some elections. This is sometimes qualified on the basis of age, for example after age eighteen, or until age 70.

topics.label: Term limits for first chamber
topics.desc: The number of terms, either consecutive or in total, that an individual may serve as a representative in the first chamber of the legislature.

topics.label: Indigenous right to representation
topics.desc: Grants indigenous peoples the right to representation in the central government. This might, for example, involve a seat quota in the legislature.

topics.label: Constitutional court opinions
topics.desc: Determines procedures for, or treatment of, judicial opinions handed down by the constitutional court.

topics.label: Establishment of religious courts
topics.desc: Courts with limited jurisdiction to adjudicate matters arising in religious law. Jurisdiction may be limited on a confessional basis.

topics.label: Term limits of second chamber
topics.desc: The number of terms, either consecutive or in total, that an individual may serve as a representative in the second chamber of the legislature.

topics.label: Age restrictions on electoral court judges
topics.desc: Most commonly establishes the minimum age that an individual must have attained before assuming the office of judge in an electoral court. In some cases may also provide a maximum age.

topics.label: Age restrictions on ordinary court judges
topics.desc: Most commonly establishes the minimum age that an individual must have attained before assuming the office of judge in an ordinary court. In some cases may also provide a maximum age.

topics.label: Citizenship of indigenous groups
topics.desc: Clarifies the citizenship status of members of indigenous groups. In some cases indigenous groups may be granted citizenship in a sub-national unit.

topics.label: Right to bear arms
topics.desc: Grants individuals the right to possess firearms and other weapons. This right may in some jurisdictions still be subject to regulation of the kinds of weapons that can be possessed, and the places and manners in which they may be transported.

topics.label: Electoral court removal
topics.desc: In cases where a judge has committed a crime, or otherwise compromised the integrity of their office, he or she may be removed from office. This may be carried out by the legislature, the executive, or another competent body.

topics.label: Equality regardless of sexual orientation
topics.desc: Requires that everyone is treated equally before the law, without regard to their sexual orientation. This may apply to both public and private interactions in some jurisdictions.

topics.label: Preferred political parties
topics.desc: A particular political party, or type of party, has a special status within the state.

topics.label: Tax status of religious organizations
topics.desc: Religious organizations are granted a special status with regard to taxation. This may include exemptions from regular taxation of income or property.

topics.label: Head of government term limits
topics.desc: The number of terms, either consecutive or in total, that an individual may serve in the office of head of government.

topics.label: Indigenous right to vote
topics.desc: Specifically grants indigenous peoples the right to vote in national elections or referenda.

topics.label: Truth and reconciliation commission
topics.desc: A special commission tasked with hearing testimony and gathering evidence about human rights violations and other crimes, usually committed by a previous regime. Testimony given in such a commission may or may not be protected from use in future prosecutions.

topics.label: Administrative court term limits
topics.desc: The number of terms, either consecutive or in total, that an individual may serve as a judge in an administrative court.

topics.label: Ordinary court term limits
topics.desc: The number of terms, either consecutive or in total, that an individual may serve as a judge in an ordinary court.

topics.label: Age restrictions on administrative judges
topics.desc: Most commonly establishes the minimum age that an individual must have attained before assuming the office of judge in an administrative court. In some cases may also provide a maximum age.

topics.label: Electoral court term limits
topics.desc: The number of terms, either consecutive or in total, that an individual may serve as a judge in an electoral court.

topics.label: Establishment of tax courts
topics.desc: Courts with limited jurisdiction to adjudicate disputes between individuals or businesses and the state with regard to taxation.

topics.label: Prison registry
topics.desc: Requires that the state produce a public registry of the names of those imprisoned. This often serves as a check on arbitrary or unjust imprisonment.

topics.label: Restrictions on minister of defense
topics.desc: Qualifications that an individual must meet in order to serve as the minister of defense. Particularly concerned with whether the minister is required to be, or prohibited from being, a member of the military.

topics.label: Duty to join a political party
topics.desc: Requires all citizens to be a member of a political party, or of the sole political party of the state.

topics.label: Establishment of courts of amparo
topics.desc: Courts that review government actions to determine whether an individual's rights were infringed or violated.

topics.label: Indigenous right not to pay taxes
topics.desc: Grants indigenous peoples an exemption from taxation by the central government.

topics.label: Indigenous right to illegal activities
